facts.raw_span: A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
parietal cells was shortened with mild degeneration
A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
parietal cells was shortened with mild degeneration

concepts.why: The patient's foveolar hyperplasia, parietal cell shortening with mild degeneration, and heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining are consistent with autoimmune gastritis, which is also supported by the patient's autoimmune hepatitis diagnosis.

The patient's normal antrum appearance, normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules in the gastric corpus, and regular round pit patterns on magnified narrow-band imaging are consistent with chronic gastritis.

The patient's red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle, foveolar hyperplasia, and parietal cell shortening with mild degeneration are consistent with gastric mucosal inflammation.
The patient's diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus is a known autoimmune disorder that can affect multiple organ systems.
The patient's diagnosis of Sjögren’s syndrome is a known autoimmune disorder that can affect exocrine glands.
The patient's diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis is a known autoimmune disorder that can affect the liver.
The patient's negative Anti-H. pylori IgG test and normal gastric corpus appearance are consistent with Helicobacter pylori-negative gastritis.
The patient's unremarkable vital signs, physical examination, and normal antrum appearance are consistent with idiopathic gastritis.
The negative anti-parietal cell antibody finding does not support pernicious anemia, however, the presence of autoimmune disorders and gastritis suggests a possible link to pernicious anemia.
The negative anti-parietal cell antibody and anti-H. pylori IgG findings, along with the presence of gastritis, suggest a possible diagnosis of atrophic gastritis.
